subject: english-language
title: Power in the Workplace
welcome_lead: Memos, meetings, performance reviews — the office is a laboratory of asymmetric discourse. Examine the speech of status.
meta_desc: Workplace asymmetric discourse, face-threatening acts and managerial language at A-Level English Language.
final_note: You have audited the dialect of management — politeness, FTAs and the soft enforcement of hierarchy.

concepts.def: Any utterance (request, refusal, criticism) that threatens speaker or hearer face, requiring mitigation.
Direct expression of an FTA without redress (Sit down), reserved for emergencies or marked status difference.
Strategy emphasising solidarity with the hearer (We're all in this together) to soften an imposition.
Strategy minimising imposition on autonomy (I hate to ask, but.), deferential and indirect.
Interactions where managerial participants control turn allocation, topic and evaluative feedback (Drew & Heritage 1992).
Erving Goffman (1981) described shifts in speaker alignment that recalibrate institutional roles within talk.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Asking an employee to redo a report is an FTA against negative face. A manager might choose negative politeness: Would you mind, when you get a moment, taking another look at section three?

Hedges, modal verbs and conditional structures protect autonomy while preserving authority.

Drew and Heritage (1992) identify institutional talk by goal-orientation, asymmetry and special inferential frameworks.

A doctor's and how long has that been bothering you? presupposes the patient's role and steers the interaction toward diagnosis — a clear power gradient.

Goffman's footing captures how a speaker can shift between principal, author and animator within one stretch of talk.

When a manager says HR have asked me to mention. they animate another's words, distancing themselves from the FTA while still enforcing it.

mcqs.q: What did Chomsky propose about language acquisition?
options: Chomsky said children learn language entirely by copying adults.
Children possess an innate Language Acquisition Device — an inborn capacity for grammar — because exposure alone cannot account for how rapidly and uniformly children learn complex syntax.
Vygotsky was a behaviourist who emphasised reinforcement.
Chomsky said children should be taught grammar from age two.

mcqs.q: What is Skinner's behaviourist view of language acquisition?
options: Skinner believed children couldn't learn language until age five.
Vygotsky was a behaviourist who emphasised reinforcement.
Children learn language through imitation and operant conditioning — they are reinforced for correct utterances and corrected for errors.
Skinner believed in an innate grammar module.

mcqs.q: What is Vygotsky's view of language development?
options: Vygotsky was a behaviourist who emphasised reinforcement.
Vygotsky believed children develop language alone through internal processes.
Language develops through social interaction with more knowledgeable others — they 'scaffold' the child within the Zone of Proximal Development.
Chomsky said children should be taught grammar from age two.
